title: Florence
completionText: You depart Florence with eyes full of Botticelli and pockets full of forged Medici medals. Venice awaits.

cards.dialogue: "You cross the Apennines and descend into the Arno valley. Brunelleschi's dome rises against the morning mist. Your gondolier on the road—a muleteer, rather—asks where to lodge."
cards.leftText: You take an attic above a tanner's shop. The view of San Miniato is splendid; the air, less so.
cards.rightText: The Locanda dell'Aquila Nera receives you well. A Hanoverian baron is in the next suite.

cards.dialogue: "Your letter of credit is in order, signore. The Bardi have served English travellers since the days of Edward III. A small commission will be deducted, as is customary—and a token for the clerk, of course."
cards.leftText: Bardi's smile thins. "Of course, signore. As you wish." You suspect future drafts will take longer to clear.
cards.rightText: Bardi pours a glass of Vernaccia. "You begin to understand Florence, my friend."

cards.dialogue: "The Granducal collection is closed to the curious public, but for a serious student of art, exceptions may be arranged. The Tribuna alone — the Venus, the Wrestlers — repays the journey from London."
cards.leftText: You sit on the loggia for hours, copying the lines of Giambologna's Rape of the Sabines.
cards.rightText: The Tribuna is small, octagonal, and stunning. You leave drunk on antique flesh.
cards.rightItem: Sketch of the Venus de' Medici

cards.dialogue: "These bronzes were turned up by my cousin's plough, near Careggi. The portrait of Lorenzo himself, signore — observe the nose! A trifling sum for so much history."
cards.leftText: The seller swears at your back in Tuscan dialect. Two other tourists buy his wares as you leave.
cards.rightText: You will discover in London that the patina was achieved with vinegar and a coal scuttle.
cards.rightItem: A drawer of forged Medici medals

cards.dialogue: "You looked twice at my sister at the Pergola last night, signore. My seconds wait in the courtyard. Florence settles these affairs at dawn, in the Cascine — unless the Englishman prefers his apologies in writing."
cards.leftText: The Count departs satisfied. Florentine drawing rooms fall silent when you enter for a fortnight.
cards.rightText: Your shoulder will trouble you in damp weather, but Capponi's ball missed your heart by an inch. He embraces you. You are now invited everywhere.

cards.dialogue: "The summer fevers come from the marshes, signore. This Jesuit's bark from Peru is dear but certain — a single dose has saved princes. Or you may trust to your English constitution."
cards.leftText: Three days in a sweat-soaked bed. You consider, briefly, whether you might die in Florence.
cards.rightText: The bitter draught works. You take notes for a letter to the Royal Society in London.
